description: React + TypeScript dashboard. Depends on FEAT-001 and FEAT-002 (API must be defined; C build need not be running for TypeScript type-check). Creates a Vite react-ts project at dashboard/, implements three screens (Overview, Backend Health, Benchmark Lab), wires them to the C admin API endpoints from api-contract.md, and passes tsc --noEmit with zero errors. All live data comes from the API; no hardcoded mock values in production screens.
steps: Bootstrap the Vite project: from Windows PowerShell run: cmd /c "cd c:\Users\HARI\Downloads\flutter\edgemesh && npm create vite@latest dashboard -- --template react-ts --yes" . Then run: cmd /c "cd c:\Users\HARI\Downloads\flutter\edgemesh\dashboard && npm install". Verify dashboard/package.json and dashboard/src/main.tsx exist.

Create dashboard/src/api/client.ts: typed API client with the base URL http://127.0.0.1:9090. Export typed fetch wrappers for each endpoint mirroring the schemas in api-contract.md: getHealth() -> HealthResponse, getOverview() -> OverviewResponse, getBackends() -> BackendsResponse, putPolicy(policy: string) -> PolicyResponse, getMetrics(window_seconds?: number) -> MetricsResponse, getBenchmarkLatest() -> BenchmarkLatestResponse. All functions return Promise<T> and throw typed ApiError on non-2xx. Export the full TypeScript interfaces for each response type — field names and types MUST match api-contract.md exactly (e.g. latency_p50_ms: number | null, state: 'healthy' | 'unhealthy' | 'unknown').

Create dashboard/src/hooks/usePolling.ts: custom hook usePolling<T>(fetchFn, intervalMs) that calls fetchFn every intervalMs milliseconds, returns {data, loading, error, lastUpdated}. Clears the interval on unmount. On fetch error sets error state and keeps last known data. intervalMs minimum enforced at 2000ms.

Create dashboard/src/components/StatusBadge.tsx: displays backend state ('healthy' -> green, 'unhealthy' -> red, 'unknown' -> gray) as a styled inline badge. Accessible: uses role='status' and aria-label.

Create dashboard/src/components/MetricCard.tsx: displays a single metric (label + value + optional unit). Renders a loading skeleton when value is undefined/null. Accessible: uses appropriate aria-label.
Create dashboard/src/components/ErrorBanner.tsx: displays an error or disconnected state banner with a retry button. Visible when the API is unreachable.

Create dashboard/src/pages/Overview.tsx: polls GET /api/v1/overview every 2s using usePolling. Renders: proxy status (running/stopped), current policy, uptime, backend summary (total/healthy/unhealthy/unknown counts), and all metrics fields (requests_total, responses_forwarded_total, proxy_failures_total, requests_per_second, response_bytes_per_second, active_requests, latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, latency_p99_ms). Shows loading skeleton on first load. Shows ErrorBanner when fetch fails. Shows policy change control: a select element with options round_robin / least_connections, a Submit button that calls putPolicy(), displays success or error feedback. All values come from API — no hardcoded numbers.

Create dashboard/src/pages/BackendHealth.tsx: polls GET /api/v1/backends every 2s using usePolling. Renders a table with one row per backend: id, address, state (via StatusBadge), active_connections, requests_total, responses_forwarded_total, proxy_failures_total, last_check_at (formatted), last_response_ms. Shows loading state on first load, ErrorBanner on fetch failure, and a 'No backends' message for empty arrays. Table is accessible: uses <table> with <th scope='col'> headers.

Create dashboard/src/pages/BenchmarkLab.tsx: calls GET /api/v1/benchmarks/latest once on mount and on a manual Refresh button click (no auto-poll — benchmark results do not change continuously). Renders: when available=false, a clear 'No benchmark results available. Run the benchmark client to generate results.' message. When available=true, displays all fields from run object: run_id, completed_at, policy, target, requested_requests, concurrency, completed_requests, failed_requests, duration_seconds, requests_per_second, response_bytes_per_second, latency_p50_ms/p95/p99. Renders null latency values as 'N/A'. Shows loading and error states.

Create dashboard/src/App.tsx: simple client-side routing using a nav bar with three links (Overview | Backend Health | Benchmark Lab) and conditional rendering of the three page components based on a state variable (no external router dependency to keep it simple). Includes the app title 'EdgeMesh-C Dashboard'.
Replace dashboard/src/main.tsx if needed to mount App correctly. Delete the Vite boilerplate files (App.css contents, index.css can be minimal reset). Keep vite.config.ts as-is from the template.

Add CORS proxy config to dashboard/vite.config.ts: server.proxy mapping '/api' to 'http://127.0.0.1:9090' so that during development the browser talks to the Vite dev server and Vite proxies API calls to the C admin API (avoids CORS issues in dev). This does NOT change the production CORS policy of the C server.
Run type-check: from PowerShell: cmd /c "cd c:\Users\HARI\Downloads\flutter\edgemesh\dashboard && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1". Fix all TypeScript errors. The check must pass with zero errors.
acceptance_criteria: dashboard/package.json exists with react, react-dom, typescript, @types/react dependencies
npx tsc --noEmit in dashboard/ exits with zero errors
All three pages import data only from api/client.ts (no hardcoded metric values in production screens)
usePolling cleans up the interval on unmount (verified by reading the hook code)
ErrorBanner is rendered when the fetch function returns an error (verified by code review)
StatusBadge renders correct color classes for all three states
BenchmarkLab renders 'No benchmark results available' when available=false (verified by code reading)
vite.config.ts contains server.proxy config for /api -> http://127.0.0.1:9090
